## Failure paths and arms (fill in)

Run outside the chain on candidate 6cd0e157 (tree 9ecfdfe3), on VMs from `topology up --fresh` plus snapshot rewinds (Ubuntu 24.04 manager, Ubuntu 24.04 agent + log receiver, AlmaLinux 9 agent; Wazuh 4.14.1 to 4.14.9). Every refusal listed left the host state unchanged unless stated otherwise; a before/after oracle (images, compose hash, journals, writer, client.keys, holds, backups directory) was captured for each arm.

**Reader modes (the three defects these arms were run for)**
- Forwarding disabled, configured upgrade with the rsyslog acknowledgement (`-e siem_forward_host=` first, then `-e wazuh_version=4.14.9 -e wazuh_upgrade=true -e wazuh_ack_rsyslog_downtime_and_replay=true`): rc=0, images 4.14.1 to 4.14.9, rsyslog PID and start time unchanged, no imfile mapped, cursor file kept, no receipt, `journals=[] writer=null`, reruns changed=0. Manager verify 11 pass / 1 fail: only C11, which is not applicable without a destination.
- The same upgrade with the 4.14.9 indexer stopped mid-switch: rc=2 with `central upgrade failed; previous images, data and availability recovered`, image ids and compose hash identical to before, rsyslog untouched, `reader-replay-pending.json` published (pending, never exposed). An ordinary re-enable without acknowledgement is refused (`pending replay requires a new explicit acknowledgement before enable`, no mutation); with it, rc=0, the receipt becomes `locally_acknowledged`, verify 12/0 and delivery 1/0.
- Interrupted writer, disabled mode: SIGSTOP the remote coordinator, SIGKILL ansible and the coordinator, journal frozen at `stopping` with the stack down. Ordinary run, ordinary run with upgrade variables, wrong resume owner and missing confirmation are each refused with rc=2 and an empty oracle diff; the documented resume (owner, confirmation, `wazuh_recover=true`) returns rc=0 to the original image ids, `journals=[] writer=null`. Repeated with the reader at `producers-stopped` (loaded imfile gone, mode disabled): same recovery.
- Never-configured reader (fresh single-node manager, `siem_forward_host=` empty, no rsyslog restart): `pilot-wazuh-heartbeat inspect-reader` rc=0 with a profile newer than rsyslog's start; configured upgrade rc=0 to 4.14.9, rsyslog PID and start time unchanged, reruns changed=0. A second fresh install upgraded seconds later also rc=0. One attempt in three was refused, see limits.
- Negative controls: enabled reader with `profile.json` touched newer than rsyslog: `inspect-reader` rc=1, upgrade rc=2 `inspect effective owned reader baseline rc=1`, backups directory mtime the only oracle difference. Disabled reader with an operator-owned imfile conf, rsyslog restarted so imfile is mapped, then a newer profile: `inspect-reader` rc=1 (`--cold` rc=0), upgrade rc=2 with no mutation.
- Bundle download: the first rerun after an upgrade (and after disabled-mode and never-mode upgrades) is changed=0; the 4.14.9 bundle is not downloaded (only the 4.14.1 tarball remains in the bundle directory).

**Central manager and agents (earlier-passing arms rerun on this candidate)**
- Preview `--check --diff` of the upgrade: rc=0, changed=0, empty oracle diff. Forwarding on without acknowledgement: refused `configured version upgrade requires rsyslog downtime and replay acknowledgement`.
- Configured central upgrade 4.14.1 to 4.14.9: rc=0, manager verify 12/0, version-probe canary passes, log-server 11/0, delivery 1/0.
- 4.14.9 indexer stopped mid-switch: rc=2, previous images/data/availability recovered, 11.2 GB backup kept, enabled reader restarted with its cursor generation retired, verify 12/0; retry rc=0.
- SIGKILL during switching (journal `switching`, stack down): ordinary, ordinary with upgrade variables, wrong owner and no confirmation all refused rc=2; resume returns the original 4.14.1 images, `journals=[] writer=null`, verify 12/0.
- Receiver stopped during the upgrade with three nonces sent: all three arrived after it came back (counts 2/1/1; one delivered twice, an at-least-once duplicate the spec permits).
- Agent upgrade 4.14.1 to 4.14.9, Debian (agent plus the manager's co-hosted agent) and EL after the documented repair: rc=0, hold or versionlock moved, identity kept (manager sees the three agents Active), fim verify 30/0, rerun changed=0, downgrade refused `Wazuh agent downgrade refused`.
- Agent route/port blocked while installing: rc=2, rescued to 4.14.1-1 with hold or versionlock restored, identity kept, journals clear, verify 30/0; retry rc=0 to 4.14.9. SIGKILL of the co-hosted agent upgrade at `installing`: ordinary, wrong owner and no confirmation refused; resume with `wazuh_recovery_owner` rc=0 back to 4.14.1-1.

**EL without the documented repair (known limit, reproduced)**
- `wazuh-fim-apply.yml -l <el> -e wazuh_version=4.14.9 -e wazuh_upgrade=true` on the fresh EL agent: rc=2 `configured external audit endpoint is unavailable before upgrade`. Agent unchanged (4.14.1-1, versionlock 4.14.1-1, client.keys id 001, writer null). The who-data socket is absent, no `wazuh_fim` watch is loaded, `audispd-plugins` is not installed.
- `ossec.log` at install time shows `(6025)` Audit plugin configuration was modified, Restarting Auditd service; `ERROR: Could not launch command to restart Auditd.`; and three `(6913)` Who-data engine could not start, switching who-data to real-time.
- `/var/backups/pilot/wazuh` after the refusal: 376 KB before, 22652 KB at +0, +76 s, +3 min and +10 min (rpm-stage about 21992 KB and agent-policy about 284 KB; rpm-stage still present at +10 min).
- After the documented manual repair (install `audispd-plugins`, HUP auditd, restart the agent; socket present, two watches): upgrade rc=0, reruns changed=0, downgrade refused, failure rescue and retry as above.

**Backup directory growth measured on the Debian hosts**: each ordinary fim apply adds a `normal-<owner>` directory that is never removed (about 28 to 32 KB each on Ubuntu); a central ordinary apply adds none; each central upgrade attempt keeps 11.1 to 11.6 GB.

## Not covered / limits (fill in)

- Single native run of the chain on one candidate; the arms above are single injections, each run once (the never-configured upgrade was run three times, see the first item).
- A transient refusal on a never-configured reader: one of three upgrade attempts on a stack about 90 seconds old and without an rsyslog restart was refused with `source FD set changed during bounded classification`. It is typed, mutates nothing and the same command succeeded six minutes later; the bounded `/proc` file-descriptor scan retries three times with no delay. Not changed in this PR; tracked as a follow-up.
- Who-data on EL is not established by an ordinary apply: it needs the documented manual repair, and a refused EL upgrade leaves about 22 MB in the backups directory. Ubuntu 22.04 (builtin af_unix) was not run; its behaviour is inferred, not observed. No aarch64 host.
- `audit-log-forwarding` Step 3 runs `augenrules --load` on every apply and flushes the kernel `wazuh_fim` watches; the agent re-arms them only on restart. Observed natively on a Debian host; the co-hosted case with both roles on one host is inferred from that, not run.
- RELP without PKI, power-loss fsync boundaries, disk-full, cold-restore replay of queued nonces, who-data attribution after an agent upgrade, agent `--check` and `--tags` runs on upgrades, mount and hardlink refusals, and combined multi-point failures were not exercised natively.
- Each failure and recovery arm was injected once at one point (indexer stop, SIGKILL at a journal phase, route block); natural faults were not observed.
- The EL arms that upgrade or recover ran only after the documented repair; the unrepaired EL arm only demonstrates the refusal.
- Network-time effects: the VM clock stepped when snapshots were restored, so cursor and receipt timestamps are not compared across rewinds.
